summary:
NASS (Never Abandoned Space Stories) is a web-based science outreach platform that collects and shares the stories of the robots, equipment, and instruments that have left their mark on space exploration, especially those that remain on the Moon and Mars today.

Its goal is to make these stories accessible to everyone, regardless of their prior knowledge, through content organized into different levels of depth, allowing users to learn everything from a brief introduction to more complex scientific and technological concepts.

Additionally, NASS brings together news, courses, competitions, opportunities, and educational applications. It provides a forum for exchanging ideas and connects the public with current space missions and their latest developments.

Through this approach, the platform seeks to preserve the legacy of these pieces of equipment, foster interest in science, and connect their stories with new learning and research opportunities.
details:
NASS — Never Abandoned Space Stories

1. Project Description and How It Works

NASS (Never Abandoned Space Stories) is a science outreach web platform developed by XPZstudio in response to the Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars challenge from the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

The project aims to collect, preserve, and share the stories of robots, vehicles, modules, instruments, and technological equipment that participated in space exploration and, after completing their missions, were left on the Moon, Mars, or other locations in space.

The platform transforms scientific and technical information into accessible content organized into different levels of depth. This allows anyone to discover the story of a piece of space equipment, regardless of their age or prior knowledge.

Its operation is based on individual informational case files for each piece of equipment. These allow visitors to learn what it was, what it was designed for, how it worked, what its mission was, what discoveries or contributions it made, and what its current status is.

2. Benefits and Expected Impact

NASS aims to bring science and space exploration closer to a wider audience by making information that may normally seem complex easier to understand and explore.

Its main benefits include:

  • Science Outreach: Facilitates access to information about technology, engineering, astronomy, and space exploration.
  • Historical Preservation: Helps keep alive the stories of the equipment that contributed to the development of space exploration.
  • Progressive Learning: Allows each visitor to choose how much they want to learn through different levels of depth.
  • Technological Inspiration: Shows how scientific and technological advances make it possible to explore places beyond our planet.
  • Access to Educational Opportunities: Aims to connect users with news, courses, competitions, opportunities, and applications related to science and technology.
  • Community Participation: Provides a space where people can share ideas, exchange knowledge, and discuss space exploration.

The expected impact is to spark scientific curiosity, encourage independent learning, and demonstrate that even machines that have completed their missions have important stories to tell.

3. Creativity and Innovation

NASS's main creative approach consists of changing the perspective from which space exploration is presented.

Generally, attention is focused on astronauts, discoveries, and mission results. NASS proposes looking at the equipment that made these achievements possible and that, in many cases, remained on other worlds after completing its work.

Instead of presenting only technical specifications or scientific articles, the platform uses a storytelling approach that turns each piece of equipment into the protagonist of its own story.

Another innovative element is the organization of content into different levels of depth, allowing the experience to adapt to different audiences: from those who want to quickly learn a fact to those who wish to investigate the scientific, technological, and engineering aspects of each piece of equipment.

In this way, NASS combines science outreach, historical documentation, progressive learning, and digital storytelling within a single platform.

4. Tools and Technologies

Different tools and technologies were used for the research, planning, development, and presentation of NASS:

Scientific Research and Documentation

  • ChatGPT and Gemini: Artificial intelligence tools used to support research, information organization, concept exploration, and content structuring.
  • NASA: Official documentation, publications, and sources used to research space missions and equipment.
  • Recognized scientific research, outreach, and educational institutions and organizations: Complementary sources used to cross-check and expand information.

Web Platform Development

  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Development environment used to write and organize the code.
  • Git: Version control system used to manage project changes.
  • GitHub: Platform used to host the project's repository.

Programming Languages, Libraries, and Technologies

  • React: Library used to build the user interface.
  • HTML: Structure of the web content.
  • JavaScript: Programming and functionality of the platform.
  • CSS: Visual design and presentation.
  • Vite: Tool used for the application's development and build environment.
  • JSON: Format used to organize and structure information.
  • IndexedDB: Browser-based data storage technology.

Deployment and Publishing

- GitHub Pages: Service used to publish and make the web platform accessible.

Design and Presentation

- KineMaster: Tool used to create and edit the project's audiovisual presentation.

Devices and Physical Resources

  • Laptop computers.
  • Mobile phones.
  • Internet connection.

5. Factors Considered During Development

Several factors are considered during NASS's planning and development to ensure that the platform fulfills its purpose:

  • Accessibility: Information must be understandable to people with different levels of knowledge.
  • Organization: Case files must present information clearly and systematically.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Data must be based on reliable sources, especially official documentation and publications from space agencies.
  • User Experience: Navigation must be intuitive and allow users to find information without complications.
  • Visual Design: The presentation must spark interest and make scientific content easier to read.
  • Project Scope: The development of essential features must be prioritized before introducing more complex functionalities.
  • Available Resources: Time, tools, technical knowledge, and the team's working capacity must be considered to establish realistic goals.

6. Scope of the First Release

For this first release, the team decided to focus on establishing the foundations of NASS as a science outreach platform.

The main objective is to present the project's identity, explain its purpose, and develop an initial collection of case files about equipment related to space exploration, especially equipment that remains on the Moon and Mars.

Priority is given to the first information level, called Level 1 — Quick, designed to provide an introduction that can be read in approximately 30 to 60 seconds.

This level presents the essential information about each piece of equipment:

  • Name and photograph.
  • What it was and what it was used for.
  • Where it was or where it is currently located.
  • Year of launch, deployment, or first use.
  • Current status.
  • One surprising fact.
  • A sentence summarizing its story.

The second level, called Level 2 — Basic, is also being considered. It will allow users to explore more information and gain a better understanding of each piece of equipment's features, operation, and importance.

As part of the initial planning, a third content format is also being considered, although its name and scope remain provisional and will be adjusted according to the project's progress and available time.

This first release aims to establish a functional foundation for NASS, prioritizing research, documentation of space equipment, and the creation of a clear and accessible information experience.

7. Future Updates and Development

NASS is conceived as a project that can grow beyond its first release.

Future updates include:

  • Expansion of Case Files: Adding new robots, vehicles, modules, instruments, and space exploration technologies.
  • Development of Different Levels: Gradually completing more in-depth content, including scientific, technical, and engineering information.
  • Greater Scientific Depth: Including information about operation, instruments, discoveries, limitations, and technological challenges.
  • Space Mission Tracking: Incorporating information about current and upcoming missions.
  • Resource Center: Bringing together news, courses, educational applications, competitions, and opportunities.
  • NASS Community: Developing spaces for exchanging ideas, asking questions, and engaging in scientific discussions.
  • Navigation and Search Improvements: Incorporating filters and tools that make exploring case files easier.
  • Expansion Potential: Developing a structure that allows new case files, resources, and features to be added without limiting the platform's growth.

The long-term vision is to turn NASS into a reference platform for discovering, learning, and researching the stories that are part of space exploration.

8. Future Benefits and Impact

NASS's future updates aim not only to expand the platform's features but also to increase its ability to generate educational, scientific, and social impact.

Expanding the case files and developing more in-depth content will allow students, teachers, and people interested in science to access increasingly comprehensive information about the technologies that made space exploration possible. This could help strengthen learning in STEAM disciplines (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics).

The incorporation of news, courses, competitions, and educational opportunities could make it easier for more people to discover ways to get involved in science and technology, moving from being mere spectators to becoming active participants in innovation.

Furthermore, a scientific and educational community would help connect people with similar interests, encourage knowledge exchange, and inspire new ideas and projects.

Expanding to include other missions and equipment would also help build an increasingly extensive digital archive of space exploration history, preserving information that could prove valuable to future generations.

In the long term, NASS aspires to contribute to a more informed, curious, and engaged society in the face of scientific and technological advances, demonstrating that space knowledge should not remain limited to specialists but should be accessible to anyone interested in discovering it.

9. Project Vision

NASS is built on a simple idea: just because a mission ends does not mean its story has to end with it.

Every piece of equipment sent into space represents years of research, technological development, human effort, and discoveries. Although some may have stopped functioning or remain far from Earth, their contributions continue to be part of scientific history.

Through NASS, XPZstudio seeks to give these stories a place where they can be discovered, understood, and remembered, demonstrating that exploring the universe also means discovering the stories it leaves behind.
